questions.question: What is Harrison Ford’s character named in The Fugitive?
questions.note: Dr. Richard Kimble, Chicago vascular surgeon. David Janssen played him on the 1960s TV series.

questions.question: Which actor plays U.S. Marshal Samuel Gerard opposite Ford in The Fugitive?
questions.note: Jones won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for playing Gerard.

questions.question: Kimble spends The Fugitive hunting which figure from the night of the murder?
questions.note: Sykes, played by Andreas Katsulas. The TV show used the same hook.

questions.question: While on the run in The Fugitive, what job does Kimble take inside a hospital?
questions.note: He needs records, and he cannot walk in as Dr. Kimble. He still ends up helping a patient.

questions.question: In The Fugitive’s most famous stunt, what does Kimble jump from?
questions.note: Cheoah Dam in North Carolina stands in. The bus-train wreck comes first; the dam is the escape.

questions.question: In what year was The Fugitive released?
questions.note: It was a huge hit. Andrew Davis directed.

questions.question: Who directed The Fugitive?
questions.note: Davis also made Under Siege. Petersen did Air Force One a few years later, another Ford man-on-the-run picture.

questions.question: The Fugitive is based on what earlier property?
questions.note: ABC, 1963 to 1967, David Janssen as Kimble. The movie keeps the one-armed man and the marshals.

questions.question: In what city does most of The Fugitive take place after Kimble escapes?
questions.note: St. Patrick’s Day parade, el trains, and a hospital Kimble should not walk into.

questions.question: In the tunnel standoff, what does Kimble shout at Marshal Gerard?
questions.note: Gerard’s reply is basically that he does not care. Ford sells the line exhausted.
